summary: Both sides render the same 60-px sky simulation — dawn glow, blue day with a white sun crossing the strip at an identical 4 px/s, dusk glow, then permanent night — and respond identically to WakeTime/SleepTime and to every colour picker, but the port's vignette is far steeper (and never reaches 'off'), its sun is consequently dimmed toward the strip ends where the original's stays full white, its cloud layer is much weaker at high Cloudiness, and its colour controls are hsvPickers with different names where the original has rgbPickers.
observations: ENGINE GAP (pinned wall clock): --wall-clock is inert on BOTH sides. Swept 1755978000 / 1755989000 / 1756000000 / 1756021200 / 1756042800 / 1756064400 (spanning >24 h) at 2 s/10 fps and every run produced byte-identical stats (orig mean 0 motion 0, port mean 21 motion 3). The pattern is plainly a time-of-day clock, so the mapping from real hours to the rendered sky, and the weekday/weekend branch, are UNVERIFIABLE from output. Everything below is judged on the simulated-time day both sides do produce; confidence capped at medium for this reason.

Both sides run exactly ONE day and then night forever: a 600 s survey at 2 fps (matched gamma/vignette) found a single lit interval on each side — orig 6.5-21.0 s, port 0.0-15.5 s — and pure black for the remaining ~580 s. Steady state therefore matches (both permanently dark); confirmed again with --skip 30 --seconds 20 --fps 10 (both mean 0, motion 0).

Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): at 20 fps the orig's day is 6.50-21.40 s and at 40 fps 6.53-21.43 s; the port's is 0.15-15.95 s vs 0.17-16.00 s. No frame-rate coupling on either side.
Both sides are seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produced identical pixel dumps on each side (orig p10/p30/p50 = 31/31/90 everywhere; port 33/45/66, 34/49/75, 32/45/67). No RNG in play.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS, ORIGINAL IS DEGENERATE: with no controls set the original renders pure 255/255/255 on all 60 pixels for its entire day (mean brightness exactly 255 from t=6.4 s to t=21.2 s, black either side) — a total white-out with no sky, sun or dawn visible. Setting sliderGamma to any value fixes it (Gamma=0.5 -> sky 31/31/90, Gamma=1 -> 11/11/46); no other control does (rgbPickerNoon, sliderCloudiness leave the white-out unchanged, sliderVign only dims the ends). The port renders a correct sky untouched. Per the untouched-defaults policy this is reported but not scored heavily; all comparisons below set Gamma on both sides.

DAY PHASE OFFSET AT UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS: with only Gamma=0.5 set, the original's day runs 6.4-21.2 s and the port's 0.0-15.8 s — the port's whole day starts ~6.4 s earlier, i.e. ~40% of a day-length out of phase. The offset vanishes completely once WakeTime is set on both (see dials): at WakeTime=1/4/6/8/12 the orig's day is 0.2-21.0/18.0/16.0/14.0/10.0 s and the port's 0.0-21.2/18.2/16.2/14.2/10.2 s — agreement to 0.2 s. So the mechanism matches and only the untouched default differs.

SUN MOTION MATCHES EXACTLY: at Gamma=0.5, Vign=0, WakeTime=6, the brightest-pixel index per second is orig 0,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,40,44,48,52,56 and port (dawn),4,8,12,17,21,25,28,32,36,40,44,49,53,57 — the same 4 px/s left-to-right traverse, within 1 px at the extremes.

SUN BRIGHTNESS DIVERGES: the original's sun is 255/255/255 at every position, at every vignette setting. The port's sun is modulated by its vignette — at Vignette=0 it reads 217 at x=4, 254 mid-strip, 211 at x=57; at Vignette=0.5 it swings 72 -> 121 -> 181 -> 220 -> 255 -> 220 -> 134 -> 72 across the day. Net effect: the port's mean day brightness arcs (26 -> 37 -> 27 in the matched-dial run) where the original's is flat (45-47 all day).
SUN WIDTH: original ~4 px above 60% of peak, port ~3 px (dump at Gamma=0.5, Vign=0, WakeTime=6). Minor.

VIGNETTE LAW DIFFERS AND NEVER REACHES ZERO ON THE PORT: at Vign=0 the original's sky is a perfectly flat 31/31/90 across all 60 pixels; at Vignette=0 the port still has p0=0/0/0 and rises 26/43/74 (p3) to 34/46/67 (p15). At 0.5, orig p6/p30 blue ratio = 53/88 = 0.60 while port = 13/67 = 0.19 and its p0 and p59 are hard 0. At 1.0, orig p0/p30 = 4/87 = 0.045 (still lit) while the port's first 6 and last 6 pixels are completely black. The port's vignette is roughly one dial-step stronger everywhere and clamps the strip ends off.

DAWN/DUSK COLOUR SYSTEM MATCHES IN STRUCTURE: on both sides dawn (t=0.2-1.0 s at WakeTime=6) glows red/orange at low pixel indices and purple at high ones, and dusk mirrors it (red/orange high indices, purple low). Setting DawnE green recolours the east-at-dawn AND the west-at-dusk on both sides; setting DawnW does the mirror. Amplitude differs: orig's east dawn peaks at 165/0/1 (p10, t=0.6 s), the port's at 79/4/8 — the port's dawn glow is about half as bright and its east/west contrast is weaker (orig west p50 at t=0.6 is 14/0/14 vs port 18/4/33).

UNTOUCHED NOON SKY COLOUR DIFFERS: orig 31/31/90 (R==G; hue 240 deg, sat 0.66 — pure blue) vs port 34/49/76 (hue ~219 deg, sat 0.55 — azure with a green component the original lacks). Explicitly setting the Noon colour on both sides makes them agree (Noon=red -> orig 90/0/0, port 88/0/0 at p30), so this is a default-value difference, not a colour-mapping bug.

CLOUDS: with the cloud colour left untouched, sweeping Cloudiness 0.15/0.3/0.6 leaves the ORIGINAL's sky perfectly flat (blue channel exactly 90 at every pixel, at t=5, 5.6 and 11 s — no spatial texture, no time variation) while the PORT shows clear moving texture (blue channel varying 52-72 across the strip at Cloudiness=0.6, changing frame to frame). Once rgbPickerClouds IS set the original's clouds appear as fine horizontal streaks and become STRONGER than the port's — a setter-interaction effect on the original's side.

CLOUD OPACITY LAW DIVERGES AT THE TOP OF THE DIAL: at Cloudiness=1 with Clouds/CloudColor = green, the original's strip becomes a fully opaque uniform green wash that hides the sky AND the sun (0/84/0, 0/90/0, 0/75/0 at p20/p30/p45 — only the vignette modulates it, sun invisible). The port at the same setting only partially tints (10/54/29 at p20) and the sun is still fully visible at 255/255/240.

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH: the original exposes rgbPickerDawnE, rgbPickerDawnW, rgbPickerNoon, rgbPickerSun, rgbPickerClouds (kind rgbPicker); the port exposes hsvPickerEastDawnColor, hsvPickerWestDawnColor, hsvPickerNoonSkyColor, hsvPickerSunColor, hsvPickerCloudColor (kind hsvPicker). Five controls with both a different NAME and a different KIND. The original's sliderVign is named sliderVignette on the port. Only inputNumberWakeTime, inputNumberWeekendWakeTime, inputNumberSleepTime, sliderCloudiness and sliderGamma share names exactly. Value-wise the pickers are equivalent (rgb 0,1,0 == hsv 0.3333,1,1 produced matching output on both sides), so this is a naming/kind fidelity gap rather than a behavioural one.

Probe (4 s, untouched) is misleading on the original because of the white-out: it reported every rgbPicker and every slider INERT (delta 0.00) and only inputNumberWakeTime responsive (delta 239). All of those 'inert' dials were confirmed LIVE by manual sweeps once Gamma was set. The port probed responsive on 9 of 11 controls.

dials.name: inputNumberWakeTime
dials.origEffect: Shifts the whole schedule; day ends at ~(22 - WakeTime) s. WakeTime 1/4/6/8/12 -> day 0.2-21.0/18.0/16.0/14.0/10.0 s. WakeTime=0 -> day never ends inside a 40 s window.
dials.portEffect: Identical mapping: day 0.0-21.2/18.2/16.2/14.2/10.2 s for the same values; WakeTime=0 also runs past 40 s. Agreement to 0.2 s.

dials.name: inputNumberSleepTime
dials.origEffect: Sets day end: SleepTime 12/18/22 -> day 0.2-7.0/13.0/17.0 s. SleepTime 0 and 4 -> strip stays fully black.
dials.portEffect: Same: 0.0-6.8/12.8/16.8 s, and fully black at 0 and 4. Agreement to 0.2 s.

dials.name: inputNumberWeekendWakeTime
dials.origEffect: No effect at values 0, 8, 16 over a 40 s window (day stays 6.4-21.2 s) — expected, since the pinned wall clock cannot be moved to a weekend. Effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Also no effect at 0, 8, 16 (day stays 0.0-15.8 s). Unverifiable from output on both sides.

dials.name: sliderGamma
dials.origEffect: Darkens/desaturates the sky. Untouched = degenerate white-out (255/255/255). Gamma 0 -> sky 46/46/93, 0.5 -> 31/31/90, 1 -> 11/11/46 (a 4.2x drop from 0 to 1).
dials.portEffect: Same direction and same magnitude: Gamma 0 -> 22/28/37, 0.5 -> ~31/47/73, 1 -> 5/9/16 (also 4.2x from 0 to 1). No white-out at the untouched default.

dials.name: sliderVign / sliderVignette
dials.origEffect: Named sliderVign. Symmetric edge darkening, and OFF at 0 (sky perfectly flat 31/31/90 across all 60 px). At 0.5 the ends sit at ~23% of centre; at 1.0 at ~4.5% but still lit.
dials.portEffect: Named sliderVignette. Much steeper and never off: even at 0 the first pixel is black and the ends are ~15% down; at 0.5 the outer ~4 px are black and p6 is at 19% of centre; at 1.0 the outer ~6 px each end are black. Also dims the SUN (the original's sun stays 255 at any vignette).

dials.name: sliderCloudiness
dials.origEffect: With the cloud colour untouched, 0.15/0.3/0.6 produce NO visible texture (flat blue 90); with rgbPickerClouds set, fine horizontal cloud streaks appear. At 1.0 the clouds become a fully opaque uniform wash that hides both sky and sun.
dials.portEffect: Live at all values with the cloud colour untouched — clear moving texture (blue channel 52-72 across the strip at 0.6). At 1.0 only a partial tint; the sky and the sun both remain visible. Weaker overall at the top of the dial, stronger at the bottom.

dials.name: rgbPickerNoon / hsvPickerNoonSkyColor
dials.origEffect: Sets the daytime sky colour. Noon=red -> sky 88/0/0 to 90/0/0; Noon=green -> 0/84/0 to 0/90/0. Untouched default is 31/31/90 (hue 240, sat 0.66).
dials.portEffect: Same behaviour: NoonSkyColor=hsv(0,1,1) -> 88/0/0 at centre; hsv(1/3,1,1) -> 0/88/0. Untouched default is 34/49/76 (hue ~219, sat 0.55) — a different default hue. Name and kind differ.

dials.name: rgbPickerSun / hsvPickerSunColor
dials.origEffect: Tints the sun disc. Sun=red -> sun pixel 255/31/90 (red over the blue sky).
dials.portEffect: Same: sun pixel 255/50/78. Name and kind differ.

dials.name: rgbPickerDawnE / hsvPickerEastDawnColor
dials.origEffect: Colours the low-index end at dawn and the high-index end at dusk. Green -> 0/165/1 at p10 during dawn, 11/101/35 at p50 during dusk.
dials.portEffect: Same roles: green -> 2/164/8 at p10 during dawn and 8/130/19 at p50 during dusk. Name and kind differ.

dials.name: rgbPickerDawnW / hsvPickerWestDawnColor
dials.origEffect: Mirror of DawnE — colours the high-index end at dawn, low-index at dusk. Green -> p50 14/165/0 at dawn.
dials.portEffect: Same: p50 18/125/6 at dawn (about 25% dimmer). Name and kind differ.

dials.name: rgbPickerClouds / hsvPickerCloudColor
dials.origEffect: Colours the cloud layer; also acts as the gate that makes the cloud texture appear at all (untouched, Cloudiness alone produces no texture). Green at Cloudiness=1 -> fully opaque green strip.
dials.portEffect: Colours the cloud layer, which is already textured without it. Green at Cloudiness=1 -> partial green tint with the sun still visible. Name and kind differ.

feedback: Rename the five colour controls to the original's names and change their kind back to rgbPicker: DawnE, DawnW, Noon, Sun, Clouds (currently EastDawnColor, WestDawnColor, NoonSkyColor, SunColor, CloudColor as hsvPickers). Rename sliderVignette to sliderVign. The values map correctly (rgb 0,1,0 renders the same as hsv 0.3333,1,1 on both sides), so only the surface needs changing.

The vignette is too aggressive and has no 'off' position. At Vignette=0 the original is perfectly flat (all 60 px at the same 31/31/90); the port still blacks out pixel 0 and is ~15% down at pixel 3. Make 0 mean no vignette, and flatten the curve: at 0.5 the original's pixel 6 sits at 60% of centre brightness while the port's sits at 19%; at 1.0 the original's end pixels are still lit (4.5% of centre) while the port hard-blacks the outer ~6 px at each end.

Do not let the vignette (or any elevation term) dim the SUN. The original's sun disc is 255/255/255 at every position from dawn to dusk at every vignette value; the port's ranges 217-254 at Vignette=0 and 72-255 at Vignette=0.5. This is what makes the port's whole-day brightness arc (26->37->27) instead of staying flat (45-47) like the original's.
Widen the sun slightly: the original's disc is ~4 px above 60% of peak on a 60 px strip, the port's ~3 px.

Cloudiness=1 should fully occlude the sky AND the sun. On the original, Cloudiness=1 with a green Clouds colour turns the entire strip into a uniform 0/84/0 wash with the sun invisible; the port only reaches a partial tint (10/54/29) and the sun still reads 255/255/240 through it. Raise the top-of-range cloud opacity to full.

Brighten the dawn/dusk glow by roughly 2x and increase the east/west contrast. At WakeTime=6, Gamma=0.5, Vign=0 the original's east dawn peaks at 165/0/1 (pixel 10, t=0.6 s) against a west of 14/0/14; the port peaks at 79/4/8 against a west of 18/4/33 — too dim on the lit side and too bright/too blue on the opposite side.

Untouched-default noon sky hue is off: the original's is 31/31/90 (R==G exactly, hue 240 deg, sat 0.66 — pure blue); the port's is 34/49/76 (hue ~219 deg, sat 0.55 — azure). Setting the control explicitly makes them agree, so just change the port's built-in default to the pure-blue value.

Untouched WakeTime default is out of phase: with only Gamma set, the original's day runs 6.4-21.2 s of simulated time and the port's 0.0-15.8 s — the port's day starts ~6.4 s early, about 40% of a day-length. Once WakeTime is explicitly set the two agree to 0.2 s, so the fix is the default value, not the mapping.

Low-priority / probably intentional: the original white-outs completely at untouched Gamma (all 60 px at 255/255/255 for its whole day) and the port does not. If bug-for-bug fidelity is wanted the port's untouched Gamma default should reproduce it; otherwise leave it, since the port's behaviour is strictly more usable and every explicitly-dialed Gamma value already matches.

Not actionable from output: the mapping of real time-of-day to the rendered sky (and the WeekendWakeTime branch) could not be checked — the harness's --wall-clock is inert on both sides, so a human should verify WakeTime/SleepTime/WeekendWakeTime against a real clock on hardware.
